head: 8226df63c268d7d521b648bcea1e655749362759
summary:
All four findings are fixed in the tree as designed. I ran the full suite on the committed build (8226df6): 400 passed, 0 failed. I also ran HookCases H-003 myself and it passed. Watch with LastRefresh missing and measure with SkippedRefreshes missing both logged 'refused ... the window has no X' and ended with exit 0 and a report. Fitness: all 62 rules hold. The xUnit cases for HF-010, HF-013 and HF-027 each feed in the shape their finding describes. The All-list test reads the real `$cases = if ($Case -eq 'All')` branch. The compressed-folder tests really compress the folder and check the Compressed attribute before asserting, and the New-File test flushes and then reads GetCompressedFileSizeW. The pin test reads every csproj under tests. Both departures (FSA_HOOK_RENAMED and TempTree.CreateRoot) were declared, and each is the smallest way to make its fix testable. One minor finding: the new test class copies the existing pwsh process harness and the repo-root finder instead of sharing them. That is the same test-code duplication SL-072 (HF-009) was cut to remove.

Second round: Round 2 found two defects that round 1 did not. (1) HF-027's refusal gives a remedy that does not work. I ran it in a scratch folder. A refused run leaves %TEMP%\fsa-window-cases (and, for TempTree, %TEMP%\fsa-tests) behind, and those folders keep the Compressed attribute. After the person runs `compact /u` on %TEMP% as the message says, %TEMP% is no longer compressed, but the next run is refused again with the same text, still blaming "%TEMP% or a folder above it". The folder that actually carries the attribute is below %TEMP%, and the refused run made it. (2) SmbLibraryPinTests reads only the PackageReference attributes and Directory.Build.props. A one-line property override in one csproj brings back HF-013's split versions and the test still passes. The rest of the walk turned up nothing new. The XML reader handles case and a missing version loudly. The All-branch AST reader fails loudly on any reshaping. The Pwsh quoting doubles `'`. WindowState's rethrow into Dispatcher.Invoke(Action) goes back to the hook thread's catch. The measure handler sets `ended` before it can throw.

findings.claim: WindowCasesHelperTests.Pwsh copies WindowScriptParseTests.WindowCasesParses' harness nearly line for line: ProcessStartInfo with redirects, ArgumentList with -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command, async stdout and stderr, a 60 s CancellationTokenSource, then Kill(entireProcessTree) and Assert.Fail. The slice also adds FindRepo twice more, making six identical copies in Core.Tests. A later fix to the pwsh harness (its timeout, stderr handling or the host) would land in only one of the two. The previous slice, SL-072 / HF-009, existed to remove exactly this kind of duplicated code in Core.Tests.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowCasesHelperTests.cs:95-129 (Pwsh) vs tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowScriptParseTests.cs:40-73; FindRepo at WindowCasesHelperTests.cs:131, SmbLibraryPinTests.cs:48, plus the existing copies at ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:190, RigLockScopeWordingTests.cs:68, RuleCopiesAgreeTests.cs:57 and WindowScriptParseTests.cs:80
findings.fix: Keep WindowCasesHelperTests.Pwsh. Move it into an internal static helper that takes the host (pwsh.exe or powershell.exe) and optional environment, and have WindowScriptParseTests.WindowCasesParses call it. Put one FindRepo beside it for the two new classes, rather than adding a fifth and sixth copy.

findings.claim: HF-027's refusal points at the wrong folder, and the remedy it gives does not clear it. New-CaseFolder's CreateDirectory also creates %TEMP%\fsa-window-cases, which inherits Compressed, but the refusal deletes only the GUID leaf. When the person then follows the message and runs `compact /u` on %TEMP%, only %TEMP%'s own attribute is cleared. fsa-window-cases stays Compressed, so every later run is refused with the same text, blaming '%TEMP% or a folder above it' when neither is compressed any more. TempTree.CreateRoot does the same: it leaves %TEMP%\fsa-tests compressed and gives the same `compact /u` advice. Reproduced here in a scratch folder. Run 1 was refused and left fsa-window-cases as 'Directory, Compressed'. After `compact /u` on the TEMP folder its attributes read 'Directory', but fsa-window-cases still read 'Directory, Compressed', and run 2 was refused with the identical message.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:188-195 (New-CaseFolder: CreateDirectory of fsa-window-cases\<guid>, Delete of the leaf only, message 'Uncompress %TEMP% (compact /u)'); tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/TempTree.cs:35-45 (CreateRoot: Directory.Delete(root) only, the same message); my run: 'after compact /u on TEMP: TEMP attrs: Directory ; fsa-window-cases attrs: Directory, Compressed' then 'run2: refused ... %TEMP% or a folder above it is set to compress ... Uncompress %TEMP% (compact /u)'
findings.fix: In both refusals, name the folder that carries the attribute (fsa-window-cases or fsa-tests, i.e. the new folder's parent) rather than '%TEMP% or a folder above it'. Give the recursive remedy, `compact /u /s "<that folder or %TEMP%>"`, which clears the folders the refused run left. Alternatively, remove the parent as well when the refusal leaves it empty.

findings.claim: SmbLibraryPinTests guards only half of the pin. It checks that each SMBLibrary PackageReference's Version attribute reads literally `$(FsaSmbLibraryVersion)` and that Directory.Build.props defines the property once. It never checks that no project redefines the property. A `<PropertyGroup><FsaSmbLibraryVersion>1.6.0</FsaSmbLibraryVersion></PropertyGroup>` in StallRig.csproj wins over Directory.Build.props, because the SDK imports that file before the project body. That is the MSBuild way to bump one project only. StallRig would then restore 1.6.0 while Core.Tests keeps 1.5.8.1, and the test stays green. This is HF-013's exact failure: it compiles, then the reflection on SMBServer.Start fails at run time in the network cases that run least.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/SmbLibraryPinTests.cs:29-43 reads only `Descendants("PackageReference")` and its Version from each csproj; :21-26 counts definitions in Directory.Build.props only
findings.fix: In the csproj loop, also assert `XDocument.Load(project).Descendants(property)` is empty for both pin properties, e.g. "{relative} redefines {property}; it is pinned once in Directory.Build.props".

obligations.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:3821: the All list goes T-004 then T-006, with no T-005 (and still no M-001). The header at :63-65 and T-005's comment at :2688-2695 say it runs only when named, as M-001 does. It is still in the ValidateSet at :90 and in $HookedCases at :110, so `-Case T-005` still runs. WindowCasesHelperTests.AllLeavesOutTheTimingCases passed in my full-suite run.

Directory.Build.props (the only one in the repo) defines FsaSmbLibraryVersion 1.5.8.1 and FsaSmbLibraryWin32Version 1.5.8. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj and tests/window/StallRig/StallRig.csproj both use Version="$(FsaSmbLibraryVersion)" and "$(FsaSmbLibraryWin32Version)". SmbLibraryPinTests checks every csproj under tests and requires both projects to be among them; it passed.

WindowCases.ps1:186-196: New-CaseFolder checks FileAttributes.Compressed on the new folder, deletes it, and throws a message that names the cause. The run loop at :3840-3846 reports that message as the case's FAIL. New-File at :198-204 fills its bytes from Random(20). TempTree.cs:30 and :35-45: the constructor goes through CreateRoot, which refuses and deletes a compressed root. The three tests (NewCaseFolderRefusesACompressedTempByName, NewFileTakesItsSizeOnDiskInACompressedFolder and ATreeRootUnderACompressedFolderIsRefusedByName) use real `compact /c` folders and passed.

tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StartupHook.cs:872-884: the Background-priority BeginInvoke body is inside try/catch that logs 'refused mode=... reason=...'. :994-1015: the ScanningPanel ValueChanged body is wrapped the same way. The third WindowState reads (:930-931) run inside Dispatcher.Invoke(Action), whose exception goes back to the hook thread and into Run's catch, not to the app. I ran HookCases.ps1 -Case H-003 and it passed. Watch logged 'refused mode=watch reason=InvalidOperationException: the window has no LastRefresh', still pressed Cancel, and the app exited 0 with a report. Measure logged the SkippedRefreshes refusal and exited 0 with a report.

drift: No undeclared departures. The two declared ones hold up against the code. FSA_HOOK_RENAMED changes nothing when unset: WindowState compares against a null Renamed, and every other mode but tree and reveal refuses the variable. TempTree.CreateRoot is what the constructor calls. The constructor itself is not exercised under a compressed %TEMP%, but the only line between it and the tested CreateRoot is Path.Combine.

FSA_HOOK_RENAMED's value is not validated, although the header documents LastRefresh|SkippedRefreshes|SkipsNextRefresh. A misspelt value renames nothing and says nothing, where every other hook variable refuses a bad value. H-003 guards its own use, because it asserts the refused line.

With the try/catch in place, a 'refused' line from the Background callback is no longer terminal: the hook keeps watching and presses Cancel afterwards. CheckActed (WindowCases.ps1:454) fails only on 'refused' lines after 'acted'. So if the app ever really renamed LastRefresh, L-001 would stay green (it never reads LastRefresh), and L-002 would fail on 'containers=0' rather than by the property's name. The refused line still appears in the hook log the case prints.

HF-010 took the design's first option (T-005 runs only when named). Its non-timing checks (the window moved, five phases sampled) therefore also leave -Case All. Validate and the person's network pass (SL-020, `-Case All -IncludeNetwork`) no longer run T-005 at all unless someone names it.
Nothing new departed from the design in round 2.

cases.evidence: HF-010 / WindowCasesHelperTests.AllLeavesOutTheTimingCases parses the real WindowCases.ps1, finds the single top-level `$cases = if` whose clause is `$Case -eq 'All'`, and collects every string constant in that branch. It asserts T-004 and T-006 are present, so the list really was read, and that M-001 and T-005 are absent. The builder's RED run recorded 'All runs T-005' before the fix.

HF-013 / SmbLibraryPinTests.EveryProjectThatBuildsTheRigTakesSmbLibraryFromOnePin loads Directory.Build.props and requires exactly one non-empty definition of each property. It then walks every tests/**/*.csproj and requires each SMBLibrary or SMBLibrary.Win32 PackageReference to read exactly $(Fsa...Version), with both Core.Tests and StallRig among them. A literal version bumped in one project fails it, which is the finding's shape.

HF-027 / NewCaseFolderRefusesACompressedTempByName runs `compact /c` on a folder, points pwsh's TEMP and TMP at it, and loads New-CaseFolder by name. It asserts the 'refused' output and that nothing is left in fsa-window-cases. NewFileTakesItsSizeOnDiskInACompressedFolder writes through New-File into a compressed folder, asserts the file carries the Compressed attribute (so the test cannot pass vacuously), flushes, and asserts GetCompressedFileSizeW equals the length for 64 KiB and 320 KiB. That is the finding's 0-byte shape; the RED run gave 0. TempTreeTests.ATreeRootUnderACompressedFolderIsRefusedByName calls CreateRoot under a compressed parent.

HF-028 / tests/window/HookCases.ps1 H-003, which I ran: it passed. It sets FSA_HOOK_RENAMED=LastRefresh under watch, so the Background-priority callback throws on a mid-scan refresh of New-LargeTree (the log shows the refused line before 'acted'). It sets SkippedRefreshes under measure, so the ScanningPanel collapse handler throws. Each run asserts the exact refused line, exit 0 and a report. It is a hand-run script, not in the xUnit suite, which is this project's convention for hook cases.
